notes: All skill geometry is hand-authored; no ASE/dataset trajectories are loaded.
Joint ranges remain hypothetical +/-pi; torque caps and gains remain the original simulation debug values.
The 2 rad/s actual joint speed ceiling is a team-provided design value, not independently measured hardware data.
Parry is deliberately scheduled for a controlled mechanical test; no perception, reactive controller, policy or learning is implemented.
The default parry sweeps through the attack line rather than stopping on it. Too-early/too-late starts and different attack speeds may fail; retain those negative results.
Virtual sphere sites award events by swept tip intersection, do not produce forces, and are identical in each matched pair.
No hit or contact event changes/terminates the attack program. Both trials run the same full attack and recovery window.
Contact force thresholds detect solver activity only, not human-contact safety limits. Rigid contact/proxy assumptions are uncalibrated.
